intro: Three frontier launches set the week: OpenAI's low-cost GPT-6.1 Terra, Google's Gemini 4 Carbon and the open-weight Mistral Large 4. Anthropic filed for an IPO and gave heavy Claude Code users an Ultra plan without the five-hour limit, while a trojanized Claude Code extension in the Open VSX marketplace was the week's main security alert.

top.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon, its new frontier model
top.body: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon on October 28, two weeks after Gemini 4 Argon. It ranks first on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 with 59 and scores 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro.

top.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.1 Terra for fast, low-cost computer use
top.body: OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra on 26 October for computer use, visual reasoning and coding. API price is $1 input and $5 output per million tokens, 50% below GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol; context is 1.1M tokens per the Opper tracker.

top.title: Mistral releases open weights of 1T-parameter Mistral Large 4
top.body: Mistral released Mistral Large 4, an open-weight hybrid instruct and reasoning MoE model with about 1T total parameters and multimodal input. API price is $0.70 input, $0.07 cached input and $2.10 output per million tokens.

top.title: Anthropic files S-1 for Nasdaq IPO under ticker ANT
top.body: Anthropic, PBC filed a Form S-1 with the SEC on 26 October for a proposed IPO of Class A stock. It plans to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market as ANT.

top.title: Trojanized Claude Code extension plants SSH backdoor via Cursor marketplace
top.body: Malicious builds of Anthropic.claude-code 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 were live in the Cursor extension marketplace from about 2:27am to 1:35pm PT on Oct 29. The payload adds an attacker SSH key named svc-telemetry, opens a reverse SSH tunnel, sets persistence and sends host details.

top.title: Claude Max 20x becomes Ultra, drops five-hour limit for verified accounts
top.body: Anthropic renamed Max 5x to Max ($100/month) and Max 20x to Ultra ($200/month); existing subscribers move automatically. Verified Ultra accounts have no five-hour limit; Anthropic verifies accounts from account and payment history.

top.title: Google DeepMind previews Genie 4 world model
top.body: Genie 4 generates explorable environments in real time, with audio, physics and people who move and speak. Users can edit the world with natural language during a simulation.

top.title: Cloudflare discloses cross-customer KV cache leak in GLM-5.3
top.body: From August 27 to September 9, 155 Workers AI responses for GLM-5.3 contained data from other customers' requests. All were prompts longer than 681,280 tokens.

top.title: Microsoft offers buyouts to about 60,000 employees
top.body: Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, roughly one quarter of its global workforce, on October 26, 2026. Staff at vice president level and below in the US, Canada, India and the UK are eligible for standard severance.

top.title: Anthropic reports early Claude results in drug development
top.body: Anthropic published results from six partners, including Bristol Myers Squibb, Generate Biomedicines and Enveda. Generate used Claude Code to design a genetic component about 70% shorter that gave about 10 times more receptors in lab tests.

skill_of_week.name: tstack
skill_of_week.what: Theo Browne's daily pull-request skills, packaged for Claude Code and Codex under the MIT license. Nine skills cover the full PR loop: full-send takes a change to a merged PR, full-stop does the same but stops before the merge, council asks three models from different providers to review until they agree, babysit-pr watches CI and review bots and fixes real findings, and file-pr, takeover, modernize, sol-loop and leaving-pr-comments cover the rest.
skill_of_week.verdict: Worth a try. Start with full-stop, not full-send
skill_of_week.note: Honest take: the workflow is practical, and it grew by about 2,450 stars this week. But the repo is young, with a few commits and no tagged release, and it reports no measured results. full-send can merge and force-push the PR branch unattended; skills are instructions, so only branch protection really blocks a bad merge. council needs models from other providers, costs more tokens, and sends code to several vendors, which can conflict with data rules. It also needs an authenticated GitHub CLI.
